Combine Permutation Tests of Several Responses

Source: R/perm-stats.R
permcombine.Rd

Nonparametric combination (NPC) of permutation tests made with the same permutations, for example the same model fitted to several responses (traits, time points) measured on the same units: for each term or coefficient, one p-value for the hypothesis that it has no effect on any of the responses, and p-values adjusted for testing it on every response.

Usage

permcombine(..., method = c("fisher", "tippett"), tests = NULL)

Arguments

...

Results of permmodels with Freedman-Lane permutations (the default), all made with the same permutations: the same observations (rows of the data) and the same seed (or the same perms) and nperm. Names given to the arguments name the responses. A single list of such results can be given instead.

method

How the p-values of the responses are combined: "fisher" (the default), \(-2 \sum \log p\), good when several responses have effects; "tippett", the smallest p-value, good when one response has a large effect.

tests

Names of the terms and coefficients ("coef:<name>") to combine; the default is every one that all the results have.

Value

A data frame with one row per test: the permutation p-value of each response, the combined p-value (combined), and the p-values adjusted for the number of responses (columns adj.<response>): single-step min-p adjusted p-values (Westfall and Young 1993), which control the familywise error rate over the responses and allow for their correlation.

Details

Each response's statistic is turned into a p-value within each permuted data set (its rank among all the permutations, the observed data counted as one of them); the p-values of the responses are combined in every permuted data set, and the combined p-value is the proportion of permuted data sets whose combined statistic is at least the observed one (Pesarin and Salmaso 2010). Because the same permutation of the units is applied to every response, the correlation between the responses is kept and needs no model. Permuted data sets in which a refit failed for any response are left out.

Several tests within one family over time or over levels of a factor (a max-statistic test over time points) are available from contrastmeans with adj = "westfall" and a permlist.

References

Pesarin, F. and Salmaso, L. (2010). Permutation Tests for Complex Data: Theory, Applications and Software. Wiley.

Westfall, P. H. and Young, S. S. (1993). Resampling-Based Multiple Testing. Wiley.

Winkler, A. M., Webster, M. A., Brooks, J. C., Tracey, I., Smith, S. M. and Nichols, T. E. (2016). Non-parametric combination and related permutation tests for neuroimaging. Human Brain Mapping, 37, 1486-1511.

Author

Dongwen Luo, Siva Ganesh and John Koolaard

Examples

mtcars$cyl <- factor(mtcars$cyl)
p1 <- permmodels(lm(mpg ~ wt + cyl, data = mtcars), nperm = 999, type = "II", seed = 1, prt = FALSE)
p2 <- permmodels(lm(qsec ~ wt + cyl, data = mtcars), nperm = 999, type = "II", seed = 1, prt = FALSE)
permcombine(mpg = p1, qsec = p2)
#>             mpg  qsec combined adj.mpg adj.qsec
#> wt        0.001 0.002    0.001   0.002    0.003
#> cyl       0.005 0.002    0.002   0.008    0.004
#> coef:wt   0.001 0.002    0.001   0.002    0.003
#> coef:cyl6 0.009 0.002    0.002   0.016    0.003
#> coef:cyl8 0.003 0.002    0.003   0.004    0.003
